stories.summary: Bengal a case apart, P 10

stories.title: Congress gets notice to move out of Lutyens address
stories.summary: The Congress party is set to lose its long-standing national headquarters at 24, Akbar Road. An eviction notice has also been issued for the Indian Youth Congress office at 5, Raisina Road. Both premises must be vacated by March 28. The party intends to challenge the notices in court, citing illegality and political motivation.

stories.title: 82nd Airborne Division to be deployed in Middle East: Inside America’s fastest strike force that once stormed Nazi-occupied France
stories.summary: The US has deployed approximately 3,000 troops from its elite 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East, signaling heightened military readiness amid rising regional tensions. This rapid deployment capability, honed over decades, allows for swift response in uncertain situations, reflecting preparation rather than mere posture.

stories.title: ‘Blood Rain’ during conflicts: The science behind red-coloured rain in war zones
'Avoid traveling if you are...': Immigration attorney on who should be concerned as ICE agents are deployed at airports
VTuber AZKi joins Japanese police to promote new traffic rules
stories.summary: VTuber AZKi has been appointed by Japanese police as a Traffic Regulation Ambassador to promote new safety measures. A key change will reduce residential street speed limits to 30 km/h from 60 km/h starting September 1, 2026, aiming to enhance pedestrian and cyclist safety. This initiative leverages AZKi's popularity to effectively reach younger audiences with crucial road safety information.

stories.title: $1M to boss: Toronto Airport gold heist accused Arsalan Chaudhary pleads guilty to $20m theft, tells court what he did with money
'Maybe they'll see worse': 2008 crisis expert names four risks that could bring down global financial system
stories.summary: Richard Bookstaber, a financial analyst and former hedge fund and US Treasury insider who wrote A Demon of Our Own Design, the book that foreshadowed the 2008 financial crisis, warns that today’s financial system is even more fragile. Private credit, AI-driven tech, stock concentration, and geopolitical tensions form a tightly linked network where shocks spread quickly. Unlike past crises, risks now arise from the physical world, energy, semiconductors, and supply chains, beyond the reach of traditional financial tools.

stories.title: Neil Armstrong’s 1966 Gemini 8 mission caught on camera: Newly released images show astronauts’ life-or-death struggle in space
HasanAbi breaks silence after Cuba outfit backlash as Cartier glasses debate sparks fresh controversy online
stories.summary: Hasan Piker responded to criticism over his clothing during his Cuba visit, saying people misunderstood the situation. He explained that many items are gifted or sent to him. Social media users had questioned the cost of his outfit. Hasan denied the claims and said linking his clothes to Cuba’s problems does not make sense.

stories.title: 'Indian man asked me to…': US-based techie says passenger escorted off plane over seat swap drama
'America will be paralyzed': Iran issues ‘eye for a head’ to Trump if US hits infrastructure
stories.summary: Iran issued a severe warning to Donald Trump, stating that any attack on its infrastructure would result in an "eye for a head" response, potentially paralyzing America. Tehran has hardened its negotiating stance, demanding an end to the war, guarantees against future military action, compensation, and control of the Strait of Hormuz before considering peace talks.

stories.title: Who was Kermit Gosnell? ‘House of horrors’ abortion doctor convicted of killing newborn babies dies in prison
Jahangeer Ali was fleeing to Pakistan via Turkey, arrested in Los Angeles; was running fake lab in Oregon
Taliban frees American academic Dennis Coyle after more than a year in detention
stories.summary: American academic Dennis Coyle, detained for over a year in Afghanistan, has been released by Taliban authorities on humanitarian grounds coinciding with Eid al-Fitr. While Washington welcomes this positive step, it renews calls for the return of other Americans still believed to be held, emphasizing an end to 'hostage diplomacy'.

stories.title: Pakistan to mediate Iran-US talks? Trump reposts PM Shehbaz Sharif's tweet
stories.summary: Pakistan has offered to host talks between the United States and Iran to end the ongoing conflict. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed Islamabad's readiness to facilitate these discussions. President Donald Trump shared Sharif's post, fueling speculation about potential backchannel diplomacy. Reports suggest Pakistan is leveraging its ties to act as a neutral venue.

stories.title: Sikh teacher challenges Canadian bill over ban on turban and kirpan in classrooms
stories.summary: A Sikh teacher is challenging Quebec's secularism law, Bill 21. The law prevents public sector workers from wearing religious symbols. This case is now before Canada's Supreme Court. It questions if the law infringes fundamental freedoms. The outcome will impact religious expression and minority rights in Canada.

stories.title: Israel to occupy southern Lebanon, create 'security zone'
stories.summary: Israel plans to establish a security zone up to the Litani River in southern Lebanon, a significant escalation against Hezbollah. Lebanon responded by expelling Iran's ambassador, citing diplomatic violations. This move escalates regional tensions, with France urging Israel to avoid a wider ground operation while supporting Lebanon's diplomatic action.

stories.title: ‘She got money and moved next door’: Miley Cyrus jokes 'superfan' Alex Cooper is 'kinda creepy' at Hannah Montana 20th anniversary special
stories.summary: Miley Cyrus playfully labelled superfan and neighbour Alex Cooper "kinda creepy" during a Hannah Montana 20th anniversary special. Cyrus, celebrating the Disney show's milestone, teased Cooper for moving next door after interviewing her. The singer also graced the event with fiancé Maxx Morando, alongside other original cast members and family.

stories.title: $1 billion fraud by US govt: Immigration expert calls Green Card ban a silent scam; no denial, no refund
‘He told me he wasn’t coming back’: Father recalls US airman’s final call before Iraq refuelling plane crash
‘US will never give up the Moon again’: Nasa unveils lunar base roadmap, nuclear Mars mission
stories.summary: NASA unveiled ambitious initiatives to accelerate its return to the Moon, aiming for a lunar landing by the end of President Trump's term and establishing a long-term presence. The agency's updated Moon strategy focuses on a phased approach to building a lunar base, incorporating commercial and international partnerships to support frequent crewed missions and sustained human operations.

stories.title: LJP implodes as uncle Paras isolates Chirag Paswan; Nitish Kumar's JD(U) says 'you reap what you sow'
stories.summary: In a surprise turn of events, Chirag Paswan, the president of Lok Janshakti Party (LJP) founded by his father late Ram Vilas Paswan, was on Monday unceremoniusly unseated as the leader of the party in Lok Sabha. Chirag, who took over the mantle of the party in 2020 after the death of Ram Vilas Paswan, stood completely isolated at the top within his party.

stories.title: Journalist's death in UP: Priyanka says state government 'nurturing jungle raj'
stories.summary: Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Monday hit out at the Uttar Pradesh government over the death of a journalist, who had recently run a story on the liquor mafia and was killed in what police said was a road accident. The Congress general secretary accused the Yogi Adityanath dispensation of "nurturing jungle raj".

stories.title: AIADMK's stern warning to those in touch with Sasikala, expels 17 party workers, OPS elected deputy leader
Single dose of Covid-19 vaccine sufficient for already infected people: Study
stories.summary: A single dose of Covid-19 vaccine is sufficient for an infected person as there was a greater antibody response when compared with those who have had no prior infection, according to a study released by AIG Hospitals on Monday.

stories.title: Bengal extends Covid-19 curbs till July 1: All you need to know
stories.summary: West Bengal government on Monday extended the ongoing Covid-19 restrictions in the state till July 1. Essential services will continue operating following protocols, the chief minister Mamata Banerjee said. West Bengal's Covid-19 tally rose to 14,61,257 on Sunday as 3,984 more people tested positive for the infection, while 84 fresh fatalities pushed the state's coronavirus death toll to 16,896.
